name: A ski week with kids in the Alps
lead: A good family week is planned around the youngest skier. How we plan one, and where we would go.
description: How to plan a family ski week in the Alps: a short journey, a private coach in your language, a day off the skis, chalet or hotel, and the places we suggest to families.
card: A short journey, the right teacher, a day off the skis, and the places we suggest to families.

text: Small children feel every hour on the road, so the easiest family weeks start close to an airport. Seefeld is about 30 minutes from Innsbruck Airport, Garmisch-Partenkirchen about an hour and a half from Munich Airport, and Megève about an hour and a quarter from Geneva. We arrange the transfer, so the first day starts on the snow, not on the motorway.

Children learn fastest with someone who speaks their language and follows their pace. Private coaching is where EverFlow began, as a ski school in Garmisch-Partenkirchen. We coach in English, Spanish and Portuguese, with German-speaking instructors across the Alps, and shape each day around the child: a first slide on the nursery slope, or a first red run with the parents. [Ski and snowboard coaching](/experiences/#ski-coaching).
Even keen young skiers are tired by the middle of the week. A morning of tobogganing, a winter walk or an afternoon in the pool keeps the week fun for everyone.

Berchtesgaden is made for this. At the [Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden](/stay/kempinski-berchtesgaden/), the local winter sports school plans the lessons with you in the lobby, and the 2.3 km natural toboggan run at Hochschwarzeck is reached by chairlift. Seefeld has the same calmer rhythm on a sunny plateau: [Alpin Resort Sacher Seefeld](/stay/sacher-seefeld/) has a 4,700 m² wellness area with an infinity pool and a natural bathing lake.

A chalet gives a family space and its own rhythm: meals when the children are hungry, a living room to play in after skiing, bedtimes nobody else hears. In Megève, some of the [chalets we arrange](/stay/chalets-megeve/) let you ski back to the door. A hotel looks after everything and adds a spa and restaurants: the [Rote Wand Gourmet Hotel](/stay/rote-wand/) near Lech has family suites and a heated indoor and outdoor pool. More in [Chalet or hotel?](/guides/chalet-or-hotel/)

The weeks around Christmas and New Year, the February school holidays and Easter are the busiest in the Alps, and the larger chalets fill early. January, once New Year is over, and March are usually quieter. For families from Brazil and Argentina, the summer school holidays fall right in the alpine ski season. Tell us your dates as early as you can.

name: Lech or St. Moritz?
lead: Two of the great winter names of the Alps, and two very different weeks. How they compare, and how we help guests choose.
description: Lech am Arlberg or St. Moritz? How the two compare for skiing, setting, getting there and where to stay, and how we help guests choose.
card: Two great winter names and two very different weeks: the skiing, the setting, the journey and where to stay.

text: Choose Lech for the skiing: big terrain without big crowds, a season that usually runs from early December to late April, and a small village to come back to. Choose St. Moritz for the setting: classic grand hotels, sunny pistes and a winter calendar full of events on the frozen lake.

Lech is a village in Vorarlberg, on the Arlberg. It is part of Ski Arlberg, one of the largest connected ski areas in Austria: Lech, Zürs, Zug, Oberlech, St. Anton, Stuben and Warth-Schröcken share one lift pass. Off-piste days are best with a local guide.

Lech is also a place for long lunches and good hotels. The [Rote Wand Gourmet Hotel](/stay/rote-wand/) in Zug is known for its cooking, and [Hotel & Chalet Aurelio](/stay/aurelio-lech/) sits directly on the Schlegelkopf slope, at about 1,500 m.

St. Moritz lies at about 1,800 m in the Upper Engadin, with the slopes of Corviglia above the village and a lake below it that freezes in deep winter, when the season's events are held on the ice. The town hosted the Winter Olympics in 1928 and 1948 and is known for its classic grand hotels.

Lech is about an hour and a half by car from Innsbruck Airport and two and a half hours from Zurich; by train, to Langen am Arlberg or St. Anton, then a short transfer. St. Moritz is about three hours from Zurich by car or train, and private flights land at Engadin Airport in Samedan, a few minutes away.
In Lech we know three places well: a hotel known for its food, a boutique hotel on the slope, and private chalets with the service of a hotel. In St. Moritz we arrange hotels on request.

Tell us who is travelling and what a good day looks like for you. We will say which of the two fits you, or suggest a third place that suits you more than either, from [Zermatt](/destinations/zermatt/) to [Cortina](/destinations/cortina/).

sections.h2: A chalet: your house, your rhythm.
text: A private chalet suits families and groups who want space and their own schedule: breakfast when everyone is up, one long table, a living room to meet in after skiing. With a chef, dinner happens at home.

In Megève we arrange [twenty-two houses](/stay/chalets-megeve/), twenty chalets and two apartments for 4 to 18 guests, many with an indoor pool, a spa or a cinema room. A concierge prepares the stay, and chefs, butlers and ski instructors are arranged on request. On the Arlberg, [pepper-collection](/stay/pepper-collection/) has chalets such as The Barn in Oberlech, with a butler around the clock and a private chef.

A hotel suits couples, smaller families and anyone who wants a spa, restaurants and a team that looks after the details. Several hotels we know have very large spas: the [Interalpen-Hotel Tyrol](/stay/interalpen-tyrol/) more than 5,400 m², [Alpin Resort Sacher Seefeld](/stay/sacher-seefeld/) 4,700 m² and the [Schlosshotel Kitzbühel](/stay/schlosshotel-kitzbuehel/) 3,000 m². At the [Kempinski Palace Engelberg](/stay/kempinski-engelberg/), private instructors are arranged in the hotel and boots are dried for the next day.
Some places offer both. At [Hotel & Chalet Aurelio](/stay/aurelio-lech/) in Lech, the Club Chalet has eight rooms for up to 16 guests, with its own spa and indoor pool, and the hotel next door.

Families with young children and groups of friends: usually a chalet, for the space and the rhythm. Couples, and anyone who wants a spa and restaurants under one roof: usually a hotel. Tell us who is travelling, and we suggest one or two places that fit, with the reasons, and arrange the stay together with coaching, transfers and the rest of the week.

name: A first ski week in the Alps, from Argentina and Brazil
h1: A first ski week in the Alps.
lead: For guests from Argentina and Brazil: when to come, how to get there, which papers you need, what to bring, how the first days go, and where we would go.
description: A first ski week in the Alps for guests from Argentina and Brazil: the season, the non-stop flights from São Paulo and Buenos Aires, visa-free entry, what to bring, coaching in your language, and the places we suggest.
card: When to come, how to get there, the papers, what to bring, and where we would go first.

text: The alpine season runs from December to April. January and February usually have the most reliable snow, and March brings longer, sunnier days. The Argentine and Brazilian summer holidays fall in the alpine high season, and the February weeks are the busiest of the year in the Alps: the good houses go first, so for January or February write to us months ahead. A week in March or early April is easier to arrange and often sunnier.
If those dates do not fit, there is the southern winter: from June to September we host in [Las Leñas](/destinations/las-lenas/), in the Andes of Mendoza, where our founder grew up skiing.

There are non-stop flights from São Paulo to Zurich and Frankfurt, and from Buenos Aires to Frankfurt, Madrid and Rome. From Zurich, the Swiss resorts are two to three hours away by train or car; from Frankfurt or Munich, the Austrian and Bavarian ones; from Madrid or Rome, a short connecting flight takes you to Zurich, Geneva, Munich, Innsbruck or Venice. We arrange the transfer from the airport, so the first day starts on the snow.
An overnight flight lands in the morning. Many of our guests spend that first night in [Munich](/destinations/munich/) and drive up to the mountains rested the next day.

Argentine and Brazilian citizens enter the Schengen area without a visa for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, with a passport valid for at least three months beyond the day you leave. The European Union is introducing ETIAS, an online travel authorisation for visa-free visitors: check its start date before you fly. If the airline or the border asks for a confirmation of your stay, we send you one.

Less than you think. Skis, boots, poles and a helmet are rented at the resort and fitted to you on the first morning; we arrange them before you arrive. Bring your ski clothes if you have them, since in Buenos Aires and São Paulo they are harder to find than in the Alps, plus sunglasses and sun cream for the altitude and warm layers for the evenings. Travel insurance with winter-sports cover is the one thing not to leave at home: we ask every guest to have it.

Our coaches teach in Spanish and Portuguese, so nothing is lost on the first morning. A first ski week starts on the gentle slopes near the village, with a private coach for the group or for each skier, and moves on to longer runs as the week goes by; skiers who already know the mountain get a guide and the terrain to match. [Ski and snowboard coaching](/experiences/#ski-coaching).
The time difference from Argentina and Brazil is only four hours, so the first day on snow can be the day after you land.
